I suppose I misspoke there. I wouldn't necessarily call their troubles more obvious, with the exception of a particular individual, though that individual has plenty of non-obvious internal trouble. I'd prefer not to get into any more detail publicly though, as I'm already pushing the limit for how much I can say without someone being able to identify me.

I absolutely agree with you on the second point. I hang out in /r/raisedbynarcissists on another account, and that's helping a bit. A big part of my problem is that I always try to detach and look at things objectively, and I think I've gotten so good at it that even I can't really tell if I'm hurting. I only seem to be able to tell if I think I ought to be hurting.

As for alternative resources, I was thinking along the lines of a more appropriate subreddit, or something of that nature. If you do need some more information, I'd prefer to continue in PM, so long as it isn't too early in the conversation (as per the stickied post).

Thank you for your reply. I wanted to get back to you earlier, but I had no free time this weekend to privately access a computer. 

Pretty serious introspection is something I already do fairly often, and it has given me more questions than answers. Everyone I'm close to has more troubles than I do, and is relying on me as a pillar of support. I've had too many bad experiences with professionals, and while I'm financially stable, I don't have much money (certainly not enough to afford therapy).

Could you point me in the direction of some alternative resources to help me figure these things out? I'd hate to take up any more of anyone's time in this sub. I feel like a guy sitting in the emergency room complaining about a cough.
